classification.difficultyReason: Combine the cosine rule with the triangle area rule and a positive exact sine value to obtain an exact area.

content.prompt: Find the exact area of a triangle with side lengths $7\text{ cm}$, $11\text{ cm}$ and $14\text{ cm}$.

answer.short:
$12\sqrt{10}\text{ cm}^2$.

Use the cosine rule to find the cosine of the included angle, then apply $A=\tfrac12ab\sin C$.
answer.worked:
Let $C$ be the angle between the $7\text{ cm}$ and $11\text{ cm}$ sides.
$$\begin{align*}
\cos C &= \frac{7^2+11^2-14^2}{2\times7\times11}\\
\cos C &= -\frac{13}{77}.
\end{align*}$$
Since $0^\circ<C<180^\circ$, $\sin C$ is positive.
$$\begin{align*}
\sin C &= \sqrt{1-\left(-\frac{13}{77}\right)^2}\\
\sin C &= \frac{24\sqrt{10}}{77}\\
A &= \frac12\times7\times11\times\frac{24\sqrt{10}}{77}\\
A &= 12\sqrt{10}\text{ cm}^2.
\end{align*}$$
